resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says CCC crews from the Doncaster Camp erected the tower in 1934; the state inventory form is more cautious and says it is believed to be a CCC build. The two sources agree on 1934, and the story reports the register's more specific wording with the form's hedge.

sources.title: Welcome Firetower (CH-752), Maryland Inventory of Historic Properties form

notes_for_editor: Both main sources agree on 1934 and a CCC origin (register says Doncaster Camp crews; MHT says believed). Name: register calls it Welcome Forestry Tower; MHT form calls it Welcome Firetower (CH-752). The MHT form was last updated 2003 and the condition and paint details are old; current condition unknown. The record's source_pages dnr.maryland.gov/forests/firetowers/welcome.pdf returns 404; the eastern-us Welcome page yielded only a header. No staffing or public-access source found, so access is marked restricted without a visiting rule. Height 120 ft (36.6 m) comes from the register only. Record's agency matches the register.
